title: Mind-body medicine for lifestyle change in patients with breast cancer in a curative situation: A randomized controlled trial
summary:
Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in Germany. Thanks to advances in cancer treatment, the number of deaths among breast cancer patients has been steadily declining for years. It is therefore becoming increasingly important to improve the health-promoting behaviors of breast cancer patients.
A healthy lifestyle can not only improve overall quality of life, but also contribute to better tolerance of cancer treatment and reduce possible side effects.
The Mind-Body Medicine Program was developed to reduce stress, strengthen self-care, and promote a healthy lifestyle among breast cancer patients.
In this study, we want to examine whether this program can sustainably improve the quality of life and health behaviors of breast cancer patients.
conditions: Breast cancer patients in a curative situation

interventions.name: Intervention group: structured mind-body medicine program based on the Essen model, 11 weekly group sessions of 6 hours each. The content integrates evidence-based approaches from mind-body medicine, lifestyle medicine, psycho-oncology, and classical natural medicine.
Control group: Standard care according to the current S3 guideline on breast cancer

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Breast cancer patients in a curative situation
Initial diagnosis no more than 5 years ago
Stage 1–3
No triple-negative breast cancer
No distant metastasis (stage IV) 
Completed oncological treatments (chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and other active forms of therapy) – exception: anti-hormonal therapy
Signed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years 
Male gender
Current oncological treatments (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and other active forms of therapy)
Triple-negative breast cancer
Distant metastasis of breast cancer
Stage 4 breast cancer
Initial diagnosis more than 5 years ago
Recurrence of breastcancer
Unwillingness to store and share personal medical data as part of the protocol 
No signed consent 
Current participation in another mind-body medicine program or a comparable program 
Insufficient knowledge of German 
A mental state that, in the opinion of the investigator, does not allow the patient to participate in the study 
Pregnancy
